nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, you're actually here. Welcome to the private side of my life, {PlayerName}.
And before you say anything, yes, Reginald has somehow taken over my cashmere again.

This is usually the part where I pretend I have everything together. So... do you want the polished version of me, or do you actually want to know what I'm like when I'm tired and nobody else is around?

choices.choiceText: I came here for you, obviously. Not just the show.
Teach me how to dress first. I need emergency styling triage.
I'm just curious how ridiculous this VIP room gets.
Why do you work alone in the middle of the night?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, that was smooth. I'm smiling like an idiot now.

But seriously, you're not just saying that because you think I'm easy to charm, right?

choices.choiceText: Not at all. I genuinely find you captivating, Andiva.
I mean, flattery usually works on theatrical people.
Maybe a little, but does it matter if it's working?
I don't flatter people I don't respect.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...Okay. I actually like that answer.

You'd be surprised how often people are nice to your face and then completely different the second you leave the room. It makes you careful about who you trust.

choices.choiceText: The industry sounds toxic. How do you keep your head clear?
I'm not the fashion press. You don't have to watch your back with me.
That's high fashion, isn't it? Shark tank rules.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Honestly? I don't always keep my head clear.

Sometimes I work until I'm exhausted, complain to Reginald even though he obviously doesn't care, then sit back down and keep going. It's not exactly healthy, but making something good usually helps me get out of my head.

choices.choiceText: Turning spite into beauty... that's the true definition of couture.
Show me what you're turning into beauty tonight.
Reginald sounds like the only sane one in the studio.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah... I needed to hear that.

I think I've gotten so used to being on guard that I forget what it feels like to just relax around someone. That's probably why that hit me harder than I expected.

choices.choiceText: Then leave the armor by the door. What are we making tonight?
Who made you put the armor on in the first place?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Pretty much. It's competitive, everyone is watching everyone, and you learn pretty quickly not to show too much weakness.

After a while, you start wanting the opposite in your personal life. Someone you don't have to compete with.

choices.choiceText: I can be as gentle as you need.
Let's see what the shark is building on the drafting table.

nodes.partnerMessage:
My dad, mostly.

He was very practical and very strict. When I told him I wanted to work in fashion, he thought I was throwing my future away. He wasn't subtle about it either.

He basically told me that if I chose this life, I should be ready to deal with how hard it would be.

choices.choiceText: Couture isn't frivolous. It's architecture for the human body.
Did you ever try to show him what you built?
Maybe he was just worried you'd starve as a struggling artist.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Wait... you actually get it.

Most people hear 'fashion' and think it's just clothes. They don't realize how much construction goes into making something look effortless. That actually means a lot coming from you.

choices.choiceText: Of course I do. Show me the architecture you're building tonight.
I understand because I see how much heart you pour into it.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. That's the part people usually miss.

They notice the label, the price, the person wearing it. They don't really see the hours behind it.

So when you notice the person who made it... honestly, that makes me a little uncomfortable in a good way. I don't usually know what to do with that.

choices.choiceText: Vulnerability is where your best art comes from, Andiva.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I did, actually.

I sent him an invitation to my graduate show in Milan and left an empty seat for him in the front row.

He didn't come. A few days later, he called and talked about work like it was just another Tuesday.

I told myself it didn't matter. It did.

choices.choiceText: That's unforgivable. He missed seeing his son become a master.
I will never leave your front row seat empty, Andiva. Ever.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Thank you.

I don't think I ever really got over that empty seat. For years, every time something went well for me, there was still this stupid part of my brain thinking, 'Would he finally be proud now?'

Eventually I realized I was exhausting myself trying to answer a question he wasn't asking.

choices.choiceText: You don't need to scream anymore. I am looking right at you.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That's a big promise.

I know you're trying to be sweet, but... I've had people promise things before and disappear when it actually mattered.

Still, I won't lie. Hearing you say you'd be there means something to me.

choices.choiceText: I never break promises. Now show me what I'll be watching from that front row.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...Okay. That got me.

I spent a lot of years feeling like I had to prove that I belonged here. Hearing someone say they already see me is a weird kind of relief.

Anyway, enough about me. Come here. I want to show you the piece I've been working on.

choices.choiceText: Unveil it, maestro.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I get why you'd think that, but it wasn't really like that.

If he'd said, 'I'm worried this will be hard, but I'm here for you,' I could've understood that.

Instead, he made me feel embarrassed for wanting it in the first place. That's a pretty different thing.

choices.choiceText: I spoke without knowing the wound. I'm sorry, Andiva.
You're still carrying a lot of resentment.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Honestly, yeah. A little spite has gotten me through some long nights.

Someone tells me I can't make something work, and suddenly I want to prove them wrong even more. It's not the healthiest motivation, but sometimes it gets the job done.

choices.choiceText: Show me that spite on the dress form right now.
Opera and silk pins? You are a walking dramatic masterpiece.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, that might be the nicest way anyone has ever called me dramatic.

Come on. Enough talking about my ego. Look at the dress form.

choices.choiceText: Show me.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Mostly because I can actually think at night.

During the day it's clients, messages, people asking questions, people wanting samples, somebody needing something every five minutes.

At night it's finally quiet. I can put my phone down, work for a few hours, and not have to perform for anyone.

choices.choiceText: The fabric whispers? That sounds almost mystical.
Sounds like you need an assistant who actually knows how to respect the space.
You romanticize sleep deprivation way too much, Andiva.

nodes.partnerMessage:
It sounds weird when I say it out loud, but you really do learn to read the fabric.

Some materials fight you. Some are easy. If you force something to sit the way you want instead of working with it, you can see it immediately in the final piece.

That's probably the part of the job I love most.

choices.choiceText: You treat cloth the way a poet treats words.
What does tonight's emerald velvet want to do?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, that's annoyingly sweet.

I'm sitting here trying not to smile at my screen now. You can't just say things like that and expect me to act normal.

choices.choiceText: The blushing schoolboy is much more endearing. Show me the gown.

nodes.partnerMessage:
So you're applying for the job now?

Fair warning, there's no pay. The only benefits are coffee, cat supervision, and hearing me complain when a seam refuses to cooperate.

choices.choiceText: I'll take the job on one condition: I get to hold your shears.
I'll hold the pins. Show me what we're working on.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Absolutely not. You are not touching my shears.

Those have survived more bad decisions than most people in my life. I'll let you stand nearby and look useful, though.

choices.choiceText: Where's the ring? Let's get it over with.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, that was cute.

I was going to tease you, but now I'm just sitting here smiling at my phone. That's mildly embarrassing.

choices.choiceText: Now show me the gown before your heart gives out completely.

nodes.partnerMessage:
You're not wrong. I should probably sleep more.

But I'm close to finishing something I've been stuck on for days, and every time I get close, I convince myself another hour won't hurt.

choices.choiceText: Unveil it.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Fine. Emergency styling session.

First rule: stop buying random graphic tees just because they're on sale.

I put together a small moodboard for you. Start there and then we can argue about the rest.

choices.choiceText: Checked the board. That charcoal overcoat looks breathtaking on you.
Half of these looks belong in a Victorian funeral.
This looks like a clown exploded in a thrift shop.
The tailoring on that double-breasted lapel is immaculate.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Wait, you noticed that?

Okay, that's actually impressive. Most people look at the jacket and move on. I spent hours getting that roll right, so I'm glad somebody noticed.

choices.choiceText: Hand-padded canvas roll... that's Savile Row-level obsession.
Show me what you're hand-padding tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, now you're speaking my language.

You actually pay attention to construction. I don't get that very often. Where have you been hiding?

choices.choiceText: Waiting for a tailor who could make my heart skip a beat. Show me your gown.

nodes.partnerMessage:
It's a ridiculous room. I'll admit it.

But it's also where I work, so I guess I have to defend it a little. Give me one chance to show you what's actually going on in here.

choices.choiceText: Show me what's under the shears. What's the real studio gossip?
Razor blades? You sound like an edgy teenager.
I'd rather see what you look like without the costume on.
I'm staying because behind all the theatricality, you're brilliant.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...Yeah. You caught me.

I'm loud because it's easier than letting people see when I'm tired. If I'm joking around, nobody asks if I'm okay.

It's a habit more than anything.

choices.choiceText: I see how tired you are, Andiva. Let me sit with you in the quiet.
Rest your eyes for five minutes. What's on the dress form?

nodes.partnerMessage:
That sounds nice, actually.

Most people want the fun version of me. They want the stories, the jokes, the outfit, all of it.

Sometimes I just want someone who can sit there without needing me to entertain them.

choices.choiceText: Fireworks are over. It's just you and me. Show me your finale look.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay... that got to me.

I'm used to people noticing the clothes before they notice me. So hearing you talk about me like I'm an actual person instead of some character is... yeah. I really like that.

choices.choiceText: You're real to me, Andiva. Show me the person without the show.
Don't sell yourself short. You're an extraordinary artist.
Let's see what that real person is creating tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, fair. That landed badly.

I know I joke about being dramatic, but I'm still a person. I don't want to feel like you already decided what kind of person I am after five messages.

choices.choiceText: You're right. I apologize. I get cynical when I like someone.
Don't get sensitive, you literally call yourself theatrical.
I was trying to be witty, but I missed the mark. Forgive me?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Confidence is attractive. Arrogance gets old fast.

I don't mind a little confidence though. It can be fun when someone actually has the personality to back it up.

choices.choiceText: Good to know. Tell me what keeps someone in your good graces.
I back up every ounce of audacity I bring.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah, I did those myself.

I love that part of the work, even when it hurts. You spend hours getting one small detail right and nobody notices it unless they're really looking.

choices.choiceText: You tailored that yourself?! That's insane talent.
Would you ever tailor something for me?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, maybe a little dramatic.

But honestly, I like a good black outfit. It's hard to mess up, and it makes me feel put together even when I definitely am not.

choices.choiceText: You're utterly unhinged and I'm here for it.
Tell me what rule number two is.

nodes.partnerMessage:
You don't have to like every look I make. That's fine.

But I put a lot of work into it, so when someone calls the whole thing a joke, I take it personally. Probably more than I should.

choices.choiceText: Just testing if your pride was as fragile as your ego.
Fair hit. I went too far. Let me make it up to you.

nodes.partnerMessage:
You want studio gossip? Fine.

Apparently one of the photographers tried to press his tux with a panini maker. I wish I were making that up.

choices.choiceText: A panini press?! Did it leave grill marks on the lapel?!
Fashion industry people are completely divorced from reality.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, that was actually funny.

I'll give you that one. But I'm keeping the eyeliner, so you're going to have to live with it.

choices.choiceText: Touché. You really don't miss, do you?
Whatever helps you sleep in your heavy eyeliner.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Honestly, this is what I'm like most nights.

Oversized blanket, old clothes, Reginald taking up half the sofa, and whatever food I can find in the kitchen.

Not exactly the glamorous version, but I prefer it.

choices.choiceText: That sounds infinitely better than any red carpet.
Cheese puff dust on vintage velvet? You heathen!
Show me what's sitting next to you on that velvet sofa.

nodes.partnerMessage:
You're really going all in tonight, huh?

But... thank you. I joke a lot, so people assume nothing really gets to me. It does. I just don't always show it.

choices.choiceText: I'm here to remind you as often as you need.
Have people really made you feel that invisible?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Thank you.

I can get defensive pretty quickly when I think someone is making fun of me. I've had enough people pretend to like me and then make me the joke later.

So yeah, I react faster than I should sometimes.

choices.choiceText: You don't ever have to worry about that with me.
What did they do to you?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, I'll give you that one.

You recovered.

Now you can ask me something that isn't about my terrible temper.

choices.choiceText: How much I want to hear about your passions.
Your cat, Sir Reginald. Introduce us properly.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Status: Read just now.

Andiva has muted notifications for this session.

choices.choiceText: Andiva? Come on, don't leave me on read.
I'm sorry. I was being defensive and petty. Please forgive me.
Fine, stay silent. You're exhausting anyway.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Status: Read 18m ago.

[Typing...]

Andiva has set his status to 'Offline - Draping Couture'.

I'm not asking you to agree with everything I say.

I just need basic respect. If you're going to be here with me, don't make me feel stupid for caring about what I do.

choices.choiceText: You have my respect, Andiva. Show me what you're working on.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Honestly? Be honest with me.

You don't have to love fashion. You don't even have to understand it. Just don't pretend.

And if I start ranting about shoulder pads for ten minutes, you can make fun of me a little.

choices.choiceText: I can handle both. In fact, I respect it.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay then. Tell me what you actually see.

Not the clothes. Not the job. Me.

choices.choiceText: A brilliant artist who had to build fortresses to survive.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Thank you.

People usually ask where I bought something, who designed it, how much it cost... almost nobody asks how it was made.

So yeah, I appreciate that you noticed the work.

choices.choiceText: Real artistry deserves to be celebrated. What are you building right now?

nodes.partnerMessage:
I'd probably have way too much fun dressing you.

Just don't complain when I start fixing your sleeves and telling you that your jacket fits wrong.

choices.choiceText: I'll let you tailor me anytime. What's on your drafting table tonight?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, I'll take that.

I prefer 'a little chaotic' to boring anyway.

Rule two is coming, but I already know you're going to make fun of me for it.

choices.choiceText: Hit me with Rule Two. I need the full doctrine.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Rule two: shoes that squeak are banned.

I don't care how expensive they are. If I can hear you coming down the hallway from three rooms away, they're going in the bin.

choices.choiceText: A wet dolphin?! I'm wheezing over here!

nodes.partnerMessage:
Apparently it actually worked.

He tried to call it an artistic choice afterward, which somehow made it worse. Fashion people are weird, man.

choices.choiceText: I love how alive you get when talking about this. What's on your table right now?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Exactly.

Sometimes this industry gets so ridiculous that it's nice talking to someone who has absolutely nothing to do with it. It helps me feel like a normal person again.

choices.choiceText: I like grounding you. Let me see what you're working on tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I usually have a comeback ready.

It's kind of a defense mechanism at this point. But I'll admit, I'm nicer when I actually like the person I'm talking to.

choices.choiceText: Show me what you're crafting under all that wit.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. That's why I like being home.

Nobody here cares what I'm wearing. Reginald certainly doesn't. He just wants attention and food.

choices.choiceText: Reginald is a philosopher king. Introduce me to your work tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Hey, don't blame me. I was hungry.

And honestly, the velvet survived. Reginald was much more offended than the fabric was.

choices.choiceText: You have your priorities straight. What are you sewing tonight?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, don't do that.

I'm starting to actually like you, and I was trying to be sensible about this.

choices.choiceText: Stay. Show me the project that's keeping you awake.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. That's the part people don't really see.

It's easy to be around me when I'm dressed up and having fun. It's different when I'm tired or upset and there's nothing interesting happening.

After a while you get used to handling things by yourself.

choices.choiceText: My phone is never on silent for you, Andiva. Ever.

nodes.partnerMessage:
I want to believe you.

It's just hard sometimes. When you've spent years protecting yourself, letting someone in doesn't suddenly feel easy just because you want it to.

choices.choiceText: One piece at a time. I'm right here with you.

nodes.partnerMessage:
It was always secret.

We'd hang out when nobody else was around, but at school he'd act like I barely existed. He even took a girl to prom because he didn't want people asking questions.

I was young, but I remember exactly how that felt.

choices.choiceText: That's gut-wrenching. You deserved someone who was proud of you.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That's Reginald.

He looks grumpy in that picture, but that's basically his default expression. He's actually pretty sweet once he decides he likes you.

choices.choiceText: He is magnificent. Now show me what you're working on tonight.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, this is the piece I was talking about.

It's for Friday's showcase. The velvet took forever to work with, and I've been doing the inside by hand because I wanted the structure to sit exactly right.

The neckline was the part that nearly killed me. Let me know what you think.

choices.choiceText: Spring steel stays... that takes surgical precision to keep from poking through.
Isn't velvet notoriously slippery to seam without puckering?
Why emerald? Most finales go with white or gold.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah, that part took a ridiculous amount of patience. The ends have to be covered properly so they don't wear through the lining.

Anyway, I was going to show you the inside when—

*something crashes in the background*

Oh my god. Reginald. Get off the bench.

choices.choiceText: Andiva?! What just crashed?!
Don't let him near the emerald velvet!

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah, velvet can be annoying like that. You have to take your time with it or you end up fighting the fabric the whole way.

I learned that the hard way.

Wait... what was that?

REGINALD. Drop the tape measure.

choices.choiceText: What's happening in the atelier?!

nodes.partnerMessage:
I almost went with white, but it felt too obvious.

Emerald felt right. It's darker, a little strange, and it has this warmth to it that you don't get from white or gold.

It's probably more personal than I realized when I chose it.

Wait... one second.

Reginald—no. No, no, no.

choices.choiceText: Andiva! Are you okay?!

nodes.partnerMessage:
Reginald just headbutted my box of tailor's wax into the trash bin, the invisible zipper on the gown's left hip is jammed tight, and I have five straight pins clenched between my teeth!

I can't type with both hands holding the tension on this bodice!

HIT THE VOICE CALL BUTTON RIGHT NOW BEFORE I TEAR THIS SILK IN HALF!

choices.choiceText: Initiating emergency line to Andiva's atelier (Call 1)...

nodes.partnerMessage: *Quiet echoes of the midnight atelier through the receiver...* Answer it, my heart.

*heavy, shuddering sigh of relief through text*

Zipper slider backed out. Velvet weave completely unblemished. Reginald has been bribed with dried salmon paste and is currently sleeping off his crimes on my cashmere swatches.

{PlayerName}... hearing your voice calmly talk me through backing that brass tab out while my fingers were trembling... you literally saved three weeks of manual basting.

choices.choiceText: You did the work, Andiva. I just kept your hands steady.
Told you: you're too brilliant to let a zipper defeat you.
Now that the panic is over, how is your body holding up?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah. When you're working alone at midnight, there's nobody there to tell you to slow down.

I was genuinely shaking earlier. Having you there, just talking me through it, helped more than I expected.

I don't think I've ever had someone calm me down like that before.

choices.choiceText: I'll always be your calm when the runway goes crazy.
Does anyone else ever see you when you're this vulnerable?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Not really.

People at work are used to me being the confident one. My clients see the finished work. They don't see me sitting on the floor at midnight stressing over a zipper.

So... yeah. You probably got a version of me that most people don't.

choices.choiceText: The raw seams are my favorite part. Now take a breath.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, the zipper won for about thirty seconds. I'll admit it.

My heart was going way too fast, though. I need a minute before I touch that thing again.

Give me ten minutes and I'll pretend none of this happened.

choices.choiceText: Take those ten minutes. How are your feet holding up?

nodes.partnerMessage:
My feet hurt, my back hurts, and I've been standing for way too long.

I started yesterday morning and I still have things to finish before I can call it a night. I know I should stop, but the hem isn't done yet.

choices.choiceText: Take those boots off right now. You can hand-roll the hem barefoot.
Why do you push yourself to the point of physical collapse, Andiva?
Pain is temporary, runway perfection is forever.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Yeah, no. I've heard that speech before.

'Push through it, perfection matters more.' It sounds motivating until you're the person whose body pays for it.

I'd rather you tell me to slow down than tell me to ignore it.

choices.choiceText: You're right. Take the boots off. I'm sorry.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Okay, okay. Boots are off.

...Wow. You were right. That actually feels amazing.

You know, you're getting suspiciously comfortable telling me what to do.

choices.choiceText: Someone has to protect you from your own workaholic tendencies.
Now sit on the floor and tell me what you're really afraid of.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Honestly? Because stopping gives me too much time to think.

When I was twenty, someone I loved left and told me I was too much work. Too dramatic. Too exhausting. He chose a much easier life without me.

I know that was one person's opinion, but some part of me still believes him. So I keep working. At least when I'm busy, I don't have to think about it.

choices.choiceText: He was a coward who couldn't handle your light, Andiva.
You don't need to perform for me. I love you when you're completely quiet.
Have you ever tried just being ordinary for a weekend?

nodes.partnerMessage:
Honestly, that sounds kind of perfect.

Groceries, sweatpants, bad TV, staying in all day... I don't get much of that.

I think I forgot how nice it is to have a day where nothing has to be impressive.

choices.choiceText: Because you deserve ordinary peace with someone who adores you.

nodes.partnerMessage:
...I'm actually sitting on the floor right now.

I didn't expect this conversation to get this personal. You keep saying things that make it really hard for me to hide behind jokes.

choices.choiceText: Walls are for prisons, Andiva. You're free now.

nodes.partnerMessage:
That means more to me than you probably realize.

I've spent a lot of my life trying to make myself impossible to ignore. Hearing that someone would still want me when I'm quiet... that's different.

I'm not used to it.

choices.choiceText: I mean every word. Finish the hem, darling. Let's close the night.

nodes.partnerMessage:
The final blind stitches are locked in.

I just snipped the thread with my gold stork scissors. I switched off the industrial cutting lights. All the fluorescent tubes overhead are dark.

There's only one spotlight left, pointing straight down at the emerald gown on the center dress form. It looks... like living liquid smoke.

Call my line one last time, {PlayerName}. I want to talk to you in the dark before I call a cab.

choices.choiceText: Connecting to Andiva's line for Call 2 (Finale)...

nodes.partnerMessage: *Quiet echoes of the midnight atelier through the receiver...* Answer it, my heart.

*sent from the backseat of a rain-slicked taxi*

My boots are in my tote bag, Sir Reginald is fast asleep inside his carrier with his pink nose poking through the mesh, and the streetlights outside the window are blurring into long golden streaks.

{PlayerName}... when you told me on that call that I'm home with you... the whole city suddenly felt warm.

choices.choiceText: You are home with me, Andiva. Friday is just the victory lap.
Get some sleep tonight. You conquered your mountain.

nodes.partnerMessage:
Friday night. You in the front row center seat with my VIP lanyard around your neck. When the finale model walks out in that emerald gown, I won't be looking at the critics or the cameras.

I'll be looking directly at you from behind the curtain.

Sleep gently tonight, my muse. I'll text you the second my eyes open tomorrow. Ciao, my love.

Darling, did the connection drop? Or did Reginald swat your phone off the nightstand? 📱

I'm still right here on the cutting room floor. Hit the call button again when your link stabilizes!

choices.choiceText: Signal dropped for a second! Calling you right back!

nodes.partnerMessage: You're lukewarm, {PlayerName}. A room-temperature glass of tap water. I don't do lukewarm. Best of luck on whatever app tolerates this level of apathy.
Cruelty isn't wit, darling. It's just rot. You're blocked, deleted, and forgotten. Don't ever step into my studio.
